solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scottish girl out to lunch with graduate in Asian city

parts.note: Isla is a girl's name common in Scotland

indicators.note: the graduate is placed inside the word for crazy

parts.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy, mad
BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl, dazed and distracted, travels with a graduate to a city in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan, a city in South Asia.

clue.text: Dark blotches most likely stop skin developing

indicators.note: something developing changes shape, so the letters of stop skin are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Pimples or dark marks are probably what appears when you stop looking after your skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots of ink are the likeliest cause of dark blotches on paper, hence the hedge in the clue.

clue.text: Lavatory, not for all, in use — then free

parts.note: loo is an everyday word for a lavatory

indicators.note: not removes the letter for 'for all' from the word use

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: A toilet that isn't open to everyone is occupied, and then becomes available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not for all' asks for U (the film rating 'universal') to be taken out of USE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose and free are synonyms: an animal on the loose is at liberty.

clue.text: Work as seamstress, maybe, for a time

definitions.meaning: to make a shift, a simple dress, is a seamstress's job
serving temporarily until something better is found

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, MAKE SHIFT is what a dressmaker might do, since a shift is a loose dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift arrangement is a stopgap, used only temporarily.

clue.text: Live target? We might pass on that!

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a quest is the object or goal one pursues

explanation.surface: Refusing a live target sounds like a nervous marksman declining the shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass on' looks like declining, but it means hand down at death.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is a legacy, something handed down in a will when we die.

clue.text: Duke not prepared to stop building tower

parts.note: raw food is unprepared, not yet cooked
to bar is to stop or block

explanation.surface: A duke, unready, tries to halt the construction of a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' reads as a tall structure, but here it is something that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbar is the coupling bar by which a vehicle pulls a trailer, so it is a tower in the towing sense.

clue.text: Cool Italian banker's thick-skinned customer

parts.note: hip means fashionable, cool
the Po is an Italian river, and a river is a banker because it has banks

explanation.surface: A trendy Italian bank's client is unmoved by criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests finance; in crosswords it is a river, here the Po.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippopotamus has famously thick hide, and customer is jocular for a character or creature.

clue.text: One piece by queen in drag, failing to finish lines

indicators.note: the one and the king go inside what remains
the last letter of the word for drag is dropped

parts.note: to haul is to drag
one is the Roman numeral I
on a chessboard the king (K) starts beside the queen

explanation.surface: A performer works as a drag queen but cannot get through the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to finish' trims HAUL to HAU; 'in' puts I and K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of three lines.

clue.text: Girl, not the first, French teacher quietly upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters are read in reverse
the opening letter of the word for French is dropped

parts.note: Gallic means French
sir is what pupils call a male teacher
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A girl, not the top student, quietly upsets the French teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' trims GALLIC to ALLIC; ALLIC + SIR + P, turned 'upset', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Priscilla is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Companies sometimes marching, sometimes standing

definitions.meaning: ... are societies or fraternities, such as religious ...
marching ... and standing ... are both kinds of ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as soldiers on parade, but it completes two phrases: marching orders, standing orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Orders are fraternal bodies (companies), and instructions that come as marching or standing orders.

clue.text: Pink slate

definitions.meaning: an engine pinks, or ..., when fuel detonates early
to slate is to criticise harshly

explanation.walkthrough: Both look like nouns (a colour, a roof tile), but each is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that pinks is knocking, and to slate a show is to knock it.

clue.text: Survived the heat, presumably weakened

definitions.meaning: to qualify is to get through a heat to the next round
a ... statement is softened or limited

explanation.walkthrough: 'the heat' suggests temperature; it is a preliminary race.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualified means both having passed a heat and modified or toned down, as in qualified praise.

clue.text: Informally, offering crowd view, after stripping

parts.note: to press is to crowd or throng

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer letters of view, leaving its centre

explanation.surface: A striptease show offers the crowd a view.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressie is British slang for a present, a gift or offering.

clue.text: Heavy weight transported by our trains once

indicators.note: the weight is carried inside the old railway's letters

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran Britain's trains before privatisation
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A heavy load was once carried by British trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy weight' looks like one phrase; split it into definition and OUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy is slang for a muscleman employed as a bouncer at a club door.

clue.text: Play being about fashion, time to bury old hat!

indicators.note: about says the other pieces go round the word for fashion, which sits inside them

parts.note: to inter is to bury
old hat means stale, past it
to hew is to shape or fashion

explanation.surface: A play about fashion where it is finally time to bury the old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' only joins the definition to the wordplay; 'about' wraps T, INTER and STALE round HEW, which lands after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winter's Tale is a play by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Stared at and, yes, cried aloud

indicators.note: aloud says the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: aye means yes and bawled means cried

explanation.surface: Someone was gawped at, said yes, and burst into tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them hard.

clue.text: Score, and I will secure this game

parts.note: a score is twenty
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gambler claims that a score and one more card will win the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-one, or blackjack, is a card game where you aim for a total of 21.

clue.text: Pepper for one's cooking gran set close to stove

indicators.note: cooking stirs up the letters of gran set into a new order
close to means the final letter of stove

explanation.surface: Pepper is used as Granny cooks at the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pepper' is not a seasoning but Sgt Pepper of the Beatles album. 'cooking' mixes GRANSET with E, the last letter of stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Sgt Pepper is a sergeant, an example of that rank.

clue.text: Battered beef so dodgy — after this?

definitions.text: Battered beef so dodgy — after this?

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Battered beef has gone off: has it passed a certain date?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: 'dodgy' signals the anagram, and read plainly it says beef goes off once this date is past.
explanation.definitionFit: Food past its best-before date may well be off, which is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Maxine wandering round out of her mind

indicators.note: wandering suggests the letters of Maxine stray into a new order

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Maxine is wandering around, mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of her mind' suggests madness, but it is a literal rendering of the Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex animo is Latin for from the mind or heart, meaning sincerely.

clue.text: Issue uniform in Officer Training Corps Cockney's in

indicators.note: the letter for uniform goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: OTC is the abbreviation for the Officer Training Corps
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in means at home; a Cockney drops the h, saying 'ome

explanation.surface: Officer cadets issued uniforms, with a Cockney among them.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney (a working-class Londoner) drops initial h, so HOME is 'OME.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a result or outcome, as in the issue of a contest.

clue.text: Carve letters in Greek and English one spelled out

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and chis is its plural
el is the name of the English letter L written out

explanation.surface: Someone carves letters in Greek and English onto stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To chisel is to carve with a cutting tool.

clue.text: Waves approaching one's teachers, meeting each

parts.note: heads are head teachers

explanation.surface: Pupils wave as each teacher approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: A head sea is a swell running directly against a ship's course, coming at one's bows.

clue.text: Smooth kid, maybe summoned to court lassie ultimately

parts.note: to be sued is to be brought to court

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of lassie

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking lad takes a lass to court, wooing her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' and 'lassie' suggest romance; 'kid' is the leather, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is soft napped leather, often made from kidskin, so a smooth kid leather is an example.

clue.text: System which pays out with interest, that's handy for shoppers?

parts.note: the tote is a betting system that pays out pooled stakes to winners
one's bag is one's interest or hobby, as in 'not my bag'

explanation.surface: A savings plan that pays out with interest would suit shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tote bag is a large open bag that shoppers find convenient for carrying purchases.

clue.text: Virginia with endless high fibre food that's good for her

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter of the word for the food

parts.note: bran is a high-fibre cereal food
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Virginia's diet of high-fibre food is good for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for her' sounds like health advice; it is applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Brava is the cry of approval aimed at a female performer, the feminine of bravo.

clue.text: Battle alone to cross Ireland, pursuing female

indicators.note: the word for alone spans across the other pieces, which sit inside it

parts.note: solo means alone

indicators.note: Ireland follows after the female

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone sets out alone across Ireland in pursuit of a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Solferino was an 1859 battle in northern Italy, whose carnage inspired the founding of the Red Cross.

clue.text: Beach where maiden wears nothing, I see!

indicators.note: the maiden is put on, wrapped inside the other letters

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
aha is an exclamation meaning I see
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A nudist maiden on the beach prompts a startled exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha Beach was one of the D-Day landing beaches in Normandy.

clue.text: Spooner's requirement held aloft, reflecting needs

indicators.note: reflecting shows the letters as in a mirror, back to front
the answer is something the words held aloft require, sitting within them

explanation.surface: Someone holds a mirror aloft to see what is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' looks like a Spoonerism signal, but means someone who spoons out food. 'needs' points to the letters inside HELD ALOFT, read backwards by 'reflecting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladle is a deep serving spoon, the essential tool of someone spooning soup.

clue.text: Excessively particular lover of old ham sandwiches

indicators.note: the ham word is placed on either side of the former lover, like bread

parts.note: to ham is to overact
an ex is a former lover

explanation.surface: An ex-lover who sells sandwiches of old ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the sandwich filling, but it is the bread here, a verb meaning overact.
explanation.definitionFit: Overexact means too precise, fussy beyond reason.
